title: Overnight Care vs. 24-Hour Home Care: Which One Fits Your Family?
description: Worried about Mom or Dad at night, or wondering if they need someone there around the clock? Here's the difference between overnight care and 24-hour care: who each is for, what's included, how shifts work, what it costs ($30 to $34 an hour), and how to choose.
end: A real person answers, day or night.

parts.head: Overnight care vs. 24-hour care
parts.text: Worried about Mom at night? Or wondering if she needs someone there around the clock? I'm Samantha with Caring Companions in Springfield. Here's the difference between overnight care and twenty-four hour care, and how to tell which one fits.

parts.head: Someone there through the night
parts.sub: Usually an 8 to 12 hour shift, evening to morning
parts.text: Overnight care means a caregiver comes in the evening and stays through the night, usually an eight to twelve hour shift, so someone's there for bathroom trips, wandering, medication reminders, or anything that happens after dark.

parts.head: When nights are the worry
parts.sub: You handle the days, but nobody's sleeping
parts.text: It's often right for families whose biggest worry is the hours between dinner and breakfast. Maybe you handle the days yourself, but you're not sleeping. Or Mom's been getting up at night, and you're afraid she'll fall.

parts.head: Awake, or resting and alert
parts.sub: Matched to your loved one's safety needs
parts.text: Some overnight shifts are awake care. Others let the caregiver sleep, alert and ready if they're needed. We match that to your loved one's safety needs.

parts.head: Someone always there
parts.sub: Rotating 8 or 12 hour shifts, day and night
parts.text: Twenty-four hour care means someone is always there, day and night. Caregivers rotate in eight or twelve hour shifts, so whoever is with your loved one is alert and ready.

parts.head: Who it's for
parts.sub: Home from the hospital, can't be alone, up at night
parts.text: It's a common fit for someone just home from the hospital or rehab, someone with mobility problems who shouldn't be alone, someone who wanders or is up through the night, or anyone who needs hands-on help all day, not just check-ins.

parts.head: What's included
parts.sub: Bathing, dressing, toileting, transfers, meals and more
parts.text: It covers help with bathing, dressing, toileting, getting around and transfers, meals, light housekeeping, medication reminders, and fall prevention.

parts.head: $30 to $34 an hour for both
parts.sub: By the level of care, on a schedule built with you
parts.text: Both are priced by the hour, thirty to thirty-four dollars, depending on the level of care. Overnight is scheduled as eight to twelve hour shifts, as many nights a week as you need. Twenty-four hour care is usually two twelve-hour shifts, or three eight-hour shifts, every day.

parts.head: Nights, or all the time?
parts.text: So how do you choose? If nights are the problem, start with overnight care. If your loved one can't safely be alone at any time of day, look at twenty-four hour care.

parts.head: Mix and match
parts.sub: Pair overnight care with daytime help
parts.text: And you can mix and match. Many families pair overnight care with daytime help, from us or from family. And your plan can change as needs change, without switching providers.

parts.head: Help may be available
parts.sub: LTC insurance, VA, GUIDE. Missouri Medicaid? caringcds.com
parts.text: Long-term care insurance, VA benefits, or Medicare's GUIDE program may help. We'll review your options at the free in-home assessment. And if your loved one has Missouri Medicaid, our sister company, Caring Companions CDS, can help.
Call us at (417) 234-8494. A real person answers, day or night. I'm Samantha with Caring Companions. Thanks for watching.
